improvement.behavior: Chromium-backed sessions now set the real Playwright BrowserContext offline state and record network-state evidence. Unsupported targets fail explicitly rather than being emulated.

deepDive.adopted: Playwright BrowserContext.setOffline was the narrowest proven route because Ferrum already owns the context and needed no new process/dependency.
deepDive.nextExperiment: Toxiproxy is the strongest expansion for service/API latency, reset, bandwidth and packet-loss faults that binary browser offline cannot model.
deepDive.protocolChallenge: WebDriver BiDi stays additive until network-event/control parity is proven against Ferrum's qualified classic WebDriver lane.

challengePass.reason: Toxiproxy, mitmproxy, BiDi, or Apple-platform adapters would add lifecycle/dependency complexity without a completed Ferrum-specific benchmark. Keep them isolated experiments until measured.

nextExperiments: Optional Toxiproxy service/API fixture: measure latency/reset/packet-loss plus clean recovery with zero effect when unused.
Compare one network fault/interception through current WebDriver BiDi support against classic Selenium Grid and Chromium Playwright evidence.
Prototype browser/service-worker/process crash injection with crash reason, fresh-runtime replay, build/runtime identity and recovery evidence.
Qualify idb/Appium XCUITest only on a real macOS host; never advertise iOS support from inspection or synthetic tests.
guardrails: Fault controls stay additive and preserve all raw network/console/service-worker/trace evidence.
Unsupported targets fail explicitly rather than silently using fake/inferior paths.
External chaos tools remain optional until same-workload proof shows unique benefit.
Linux, Windows, browser matrix, MV3 restart, Spaces, Workbench, packaged desktop, Lightpanda, WebDriver Grid and Android/Appium gates remain protected.
